title: Durable Agent fails when using custom state store name
body:
**Description**

As a developer, I want to configure the durable agent to use a state store with a custom name (e.g., statestore2) so that I can align with existing Dapr component configurations. Currently, when the state store name is changed from the default statestore to another valid component name, the agent fails to start with an error: 


```
INFO:dapr_agents.agents.durableagent.agent:Instance 1f531f207908453fa21dbe203f616f0e: workflow_name=None, current_workflow_name=ToolCallingWorkflow
== APP - durable-agent-headless2 == INFO:dapr_agents.agents.durableagent.agent:Instance ce5201e24fda4b99a5b04aa067a56546: workflow_name=ToolCallingWorkflow, current_workflow_name=ToolCallingWorkflow
== APP - durable-agent-headless2 == INFO:dapr_agents.agents.durableagent.agent:Loaded current workflow instance ID from state: ce5201e24fda4b99a5b04aa067a56546
== APP - durable-agent-headless2 == INFO:dapr_agents.agents.durableagent.agent:Starting workflow runtime...
== APP - durable-agent-headless2 == INFO:dapr_agents.service.fastapi.base:TravelBuddy-Headless FastAPI server initialized on port 8001 with CORS settings.
== APP - durable-agent-headless2 == Error starting service: <_InactiveRpcError of RPC that terminated with:
== APP - durable-agent-headless2 == 	status = StatusCode.INVALID_ARGUMENT
== APP - durable-agent-headless2 == 	details = "state store statestore is not found"
== APP - durable-agent-headless2 == 	debug_error_string = "UNKNOWN:Error received from peer ipv4:127.0.0.1:60589 {grpc_status:3, grpc_message:"state store statestore is not found"}"
== APP - durable-agent-headless2 == >
```

linked_prs.title: fix: decouple memory + state to work with one and/or both

-        # Add the tool message to the agent's memory

@@ -850,8 +867,9 @@ async def process_broadcast_message(self, message: BroadcastMessage):

             agent_msg = DurableAgentMessage(**message.model_dump())
@@ -920,15 +938,18 @@ def _construct_messages_with_instance_history(

         long_term_memory_data = self.state.get("chat_history", [])
